stories.title: The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal
stories.summary: Within days, Huang's status as a seemingly untouchable figure leading the global tech race has crumbled.
stories.contentStatus: Freely readable article text extracted from publisher page
stories.body:
Published 12 November 2026, 14:18 GMT

Jensen Huang, known for sporting a black leather jacket to shareholder events, appeared to have it all. He was courted by leaders in both Washington and Beijing, worshipped by investors and seen as a loyal family man. But a rockstar approach to his personal life has ultimately led to his resignation.

The 63-year-old has been married since 1985, long before the foundation of Nvidia, the company that propelled him to tech stardom.

He is known as a workaholic and a demanding manager, with high standards for those who worked for him, which included his own children, promoted within the company. But he has seen his personal reputation go into free fall this week, undone by romantic entanglements, that throw doubt on his focus and his judgement.

On Thursday he resigned following back-to-back revelations of two affairs. News of the first - a relationship with a businesswoman, alleged to be a Chinese spy - ricocheted around the world, raising eyebrows among investors. It was followed on Wednesday by reports that the tech boss had also had an affair with an Nvidia colleague.

His departure creates uncertainty in the global stock market, which was already knocked-off balance in recent weeks. Nvidia is a linchpin in the US's race for technology leadership with China.

Huang may not be a household name on the same level as Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg.

But his role in the tech industry, especially in relation to the explosion of artificial intelligence in the last three years, may prove more consequential. Nvidia dominates the market for the microchips, which are used to power the new technology.

The company, which is still valued at nearly $4 trillion despite recent events, is at the centre of the AI race between the US and China, the world's tech and economic powerhouses.

Huang has had access to the seats of political power on an unrivalled scale, being courted by both US President Donald Trump and China's President XI Jinping.

His remarkable rise to the top of his profession has led to him being dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech" and seen him amass an estimated fortune of $145bn (£109bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

Despite always donning his trademark all-black outfits and playful approach to investor presentations, Huang has worked for years to present himself as a family man, someone who exemplified the American Dream.

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang and his family moved to the west coast of the US when he was nine years old. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.

It was at college where he met his wife, Lori Mills. The pair were lab partners and married in 1985, eight years before Huang founded Nvidia.

They have two children, Madison and Spencer, who now both work at their father's firm.

He worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia. Known as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan, he has a reputation for having incredibly high standards for his staff.

The company became a key provider of computer chips and circuits used for gaming before it expanded in direction and entered the world of AI. It now creates the key processing chips used to power the growing technology.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after tech giant rocked by second affair allegation

Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive? Published 1 hour ago

Huang has hailed AI as a "new industrial revolution" that is on par with the advent of electricity.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on the Jensen Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.

The Nvidia co-founder has a famously close relationship with Trump. At a recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Huang and Musk.

It was no surprise that Huang was at the top table. Companies using Nvidia's chips include Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, SpaceX, Tesla, OpenAI and Anthropic.

In essence, Huang's customer base includes the biggest firms on the planet and they are spending plenty on Nvidia's products.

This intertwining of companies means that the negative impact being felt by Nvidia, on the stock market for example, could perhaps have wider implications on other companies and the wider economy.

Witt told the BBC that Jensen Huang had gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, and that it was "very important to him".

"He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," he added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad."

After the revelations of the first affair, Huang admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting their family.

Trump, as well as other leaders in the AI tech industry, had backed Huang to continue in his role at Nvidia. The president described him as "honourable".

Watch: What we know so far about Nvidia CEO resignation

Published 9 November 2026

One of the AI industry's most important figures has resigned amid allegations that he had extramarital affairs with two women - one a suspected Chinese spy and the other a company executive.

Chip-maker Nvidia hired a major law firm earlier this week to investigate CEO Jensen Huang's reported relationship with a woman who was allegedly a Chinese intelligence asset.

Now he has resigned after its stocks plummeted on Wednesday following US media reports about a second alleged affair.

Huang admitted , external earlier this week to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and he apologised for hurting her and their children.

Here is what we know about the affair and why it matters.

Nvidia stocks plummet in US after CEO Jensen Huang quits in wake of affair with suspected Chinese spy

How was Huang removed?

Nvidia's board met on Wednesday evening to decide whether its CEO should remain with the company.

It had 11 directors on its board, including Huang. The firm's CEO could be removed with or without cause by a majority vote of directors.

But that wasn't in the end needed - the board instead announced Huang had resigned as president, CEO and board member.

It thanked him for his "immeasurable contributions" to Nvidia, which it said were "profound".

There was no mention of the accusations of adultery.

Who will replace him?

Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO .

It is less clear is who will replace Huang on a permanent basis.

One possibility is Nvidia co-founder Chris Malachowsky. He has been at the company as long as Huang, and for years led its product engineering work.

Huang's children, Spencer and Madison, and son-in-law Nico Caprez also work at Nvidia in senior roles, but they are relatively young and inexperienced.

And there is also the option of Ian Buck, who runs high-performance computing at the firm. He developed the technology which allowed graphics cards to be used for other computing tasks, which enabled Nvidia to capitalise on the growth of AI.

What we know about Huang's affairs

A New York Times report at the weekend revealed Jensen Huang had a close relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who US intelligence officials believed was a spy for Beijing.

She had previously been photographed with him on several occasions.

The tech giant's board of directors launched an independent external investigation on Sunday following the reports. They earlier said Huang's interactions with the woman were "not unusual or unexpected".

Then on Wednesday, the New York Times reported Huang also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him.

She did not respond to the BBC's request for comment.

Who is Jensen Huang?

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Jensen Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the west coast of the US.

He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.

He worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia.

Known as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan and once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech" , he has a reputation as a workaholic with incredibly high standards for his staff.

He has an estimated fortune of $155bn (£115bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on the Jensen Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.

The Nvidia co-founder has a famously close relationship with US President Donald Trump.

At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Huang.

To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.

This video can not be played

Watch: Who is suspected Chinese spy at centre of Nvidia affair investigation?

Who is Alice Huang?

Jensen Huang (left) and Alice Huang - also known as Huang Le - at an event

US officials believed Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reported , external .

She was a top executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed between March and November 2023.

Her company had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, which the firm said had been investigated and debunked.

However, Megaspeed is under investigation by the Singaporean government regarding previous allegations that the company was circumventing US sanctions on the export of Nvidia's high-end chips.

The BBC has contacted Megaspeed for comment.

It remains unclear what, if any, intelligence Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly gathered and passed to Beijing.

When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not.

China has rejected the spying allegations as "entirely groundless".

Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy Published 2 days ago

Zoe Kleinman: Nvidia CEO's affair will cause ripples across US and beyond Published 2 days ago

Nvidia hires major New York law firm to investigate Jensen Huang affair Published 1 day ago

Why does it matter?

Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world - so the slump in its value which followed Huang's resignation hits investors large and small.

The firm is also at the heart of US and China's AI race , which is why the billionaire's affair has sparked national security fears among US lawmakers.

Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the concern is if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities.

The US advantage is in large part because of companies like Nvidia, working with producers such as the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips.

Since 2022, the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security.

This means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Huang once saying Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero.

He has engaged in shuttle diplomacy between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way.

The revelations may explain why Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to sell all but its most advanced chips to China .

Nvidia boss Jensen Huang and US President Donald Trump at the White House

What investigations are now under way?

After news broke out about the first affair, Nvidia launched an independent investigation and hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.

It will be led by Joon Kim, a former US Attorney for New York's Southern District who is now a litigation partner at the law firm.

US President Donald Trump said the FBI was investigating the scandal, adding that Huang told him he had been unaware the woman he was with was a spy.

Huang has also been asked to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees on 18 November, but has yet to say he will comply.

What is Nvidia and how important is it?

There is no clear successor for Jensen Huang at Nvidia

Founded by Huang and fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993, the company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for gaming.

Eventually it changed focus to AI, a field it now dominates .

Huang rescued Nvidia from bankruptcy on more than one occasion, and took risks on AI a long time before the rest of the world did, effectively building the infrastructure from scratch.

He bet on AI at a time when "there were no customers for the stuff he was building", Witt told the BBC.

Every notable tech company building AI tools and infrastructure like Amazon, Google and Microsoft now use Nvidia chips.

Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world.

Who is Jensen Huang's wife?

Lori Huang and her husband at a state dinner by Trump for his Chinese President Xi Jinping

Jensen Huang met his future wife Lori Mills at Oregon State University while studying electrical engineering in the early 1980s. The pair were lab partners.

They married in 1985 and have two children, Madison and Spencer.

Earlier this week, Huang admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children.

In 2007, the couple founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation. The charitable fund has seen its assets surge in recent years, driven by the soaring value of Nvidia shares, and is estimated to be worth more than $9bn.

Its donations include tens of millions of dollars to engineering programmes at Oregon State and Stanford University.

Witt told the BBC that Jensen Huang has gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, adding: "That's very important to him."

"He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," he added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family.

"But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad."

The AI chip boss’s actions raise urgent questions about corporate influence, national security and the US president’s willingness to listen to intelligence warnings

I t could be the plot of a spy thriller. One of the most powerful figures in the AI revolution admitted to having an affair with a Chinese businesswomen said to have passed intelligence to Beijing. When Donald Trump was briefed about the Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang’s liaisons with Alice Huang, he took no action. Perhaps he thought only marriage vows had been broken. Or perhaps Mr Trump was willing to overlook the conduct of a friend who championed his unpopular datacentre expansion, whose company donated to his White House ballroom and who echoed his opposition to AI safeguards against expert advice.

Nvidia became the cornerstone of AI by supplying brute computing power. As tech giants scrambled for the firm’s graphics processing units (GPUs), Mr Huang sold the picks and shovels for the AI gold rush – and amassed a $160bn fortune. When China joined the race for tech supremacy, Nvidia’s microchips became a national security issue. In October 2022, the US slapped export controls on GPU sales to China. Thirty months later, Nvidia was effectively banned from selling to Beijing. Mr Huang lobbied for looser controls. Such was his sway with Mr Trump that the White House scrapped Biden-era global AI chip restrictions and then permitted sales of Nvidia’s prized H200 processors to Chinese customers.

Democrats, buoyed by their midterms’ success, will be looking for answers. Asked whether he should have acted on the intelligence, the president replied: “ No, I don’t think so. ” That makes the question of his reasons unavoidable. There could be trouble at Mr Trump’s commerce department if it backed Mr Huang’s policy agenda and loosened export controls despite knowing of his affair with a Chinese spy. Reports suggest that the commerce department’s probe was halted after Nvidia called investigators. Congress clearly has grounds to investigate whether the Trump administration knowingly disregarded a foreign intelligence threat. Whatever happens next, Mr Huang’s admission is likely to be the beginning, not the end, of the saga.

Rumours had swirled for months that Nvidia’s boss had been in a “ special relationship ” with Ms Huang – an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that in 2025 was revealed to be under investigation for suspected diversion of restricted Nvidia chips to China. What makes this extraordinary is the possibility that Mr Huang’s romantic and commercial relationship exposed him to a Chinese intelligence operation. In May, analysts at Culper Research argued that Megaspeed brought Nvidia substantial revenues, allegedly backed by Chinese financing. Then Nividia’s boss publicly defended Megaspeed while secretly conducting an affair with its top executive. More than $300bn was wiped off Nvidia’s valuation as soon as Wall Street opened.

Industrial espionage is nothing new. Richer nations often block the export of their commercial secrets to prevent others from catching up . These challengers often go to extraordinary lengths to obtain new technology. Historically, diplomatic or military so-called honeytraps – spies sent to seduce victims to gain confidential information – have been more common than commercial ones. But in 2008, British spy agencies accused Beijing of a campaign to target businesses, using sex to pressure targets into cooperating. Whether that has happened here is unknown. But a president who promised to get tough on China needs to explain why his administration eased chip export controls despite warnings that the businessman lobbying for it might be compromised.

stories.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns over scandal, replaced by CFO Colette Kress on interim basis

Nvidia’s long-time boss Jensen Huang has stepped down over the scandal, and the company has appointed finance chief Colette Kress as interim chief executive.

The company issued this statement just now, after its board met last night:

double quotation mark The Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately. Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates.

Bloomberg’s chief political correspondent is reporting that the former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving.

In an X post, Annmarie Hordern said:

double quotation mark House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast told reporters Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving.

For the time being at least though, Colette Kress is stepping up as the company’s interim CEO.

So what do we know about the former CFO?

Well, in her CFO role, Kress was a key architect for financing deals with many of the Nvidia’s biggest customers - which today include the likes of other AI titans, such as Anthropic and CoreWeave.

Kress has a long resume in the tech world. Prior to joining Nvidia, Kress worked at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments in a variety of roles, according to her executive bio on the company’s website.

Trump says former Apple CEO Cook should replace Huang at Nvidia

US president Donald ⁠Trump said on Thursday that former Apple chief executive ⁠Tim Cook should ⁠replace ​Jensen Huang as the CEO of Nvidia.

“NOW THAT Nvidia ⁠CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there ⁠is only one man to take ​his place - ‌TIM COOK of Apple,” ‌Trump said on social media. “A Legend ‌replaces a Legend!” he added.

Cook stepped down after a 15-year stint as Apple’s CEO in September and is now executive chairman at the iPhone-maker.

Meanwhile, Daniela Hathorn, a senior market analyst at Capital.com, has said that investors have been left “concerned” over the change of leadership at Nvidia .

She said that although the interim appointment of Colette Kress will “provide continuity” for the firm, it remains to be seen if Nvidia will be able to keep pace with its rivals.

Hathorn said:

double quotation mark The main concern for investors is the uncertainty following a change of leadership, especially one with a lack of planning like this one. However, the key-man risk is significant, but it shouldn’t be confused with the company’s entire investment case. Huang has been instrumental in Nvidia’s transformation into the dominant supplier of AI computing infrastructure, and his departure creates uncertainty around strategy, execution and relationships with major customers. But Nvidia’s technological advantages, CUDA software ecosystem and substantial order book do not disappear with its CEO. The appointment of CFO Colette Kress provides some continuity, although investors will want reassurance that the broader leadership team can maintain Nvidia’s pace of innovation and defend its market position.

She added that Nvidia’s recovery today “looks partly driven by bargain hunting after an aggressive selloff, with some investors seemingly betting that Nvidia’s competitive advantages, strong AI demand and established customer relationships will survive a leadership transition.”

Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at the the UK’s largest non-advisory investment service Wealth Club, said Nvidia’s board “clearly wanted to disassociate with Jensen Huang”.

In analysis earlier today, she said:

double quotation mark Even Jensen Huang’s superstar status could not eclipse the deep damage the scandal has wreaked on the Nvidia’s reputation. Even tech icons of his stature are not immune to being acountable to corporate responsibility. The emergence of the second affair, this one rumoured to be with an employee, appears to have been the last straw for the board. With the firm facing so many investigations – launched by the FBI and from Capitol hill, the board clearly wants to disassociate the company from Huang’s actions as much as possible.

Streeter added that interim CEO Colette Kress is “seen as a safe pair of hands” and that she has “clearly been brought in to steady the ship”.

However, she warned:

double quotation mark But she lacks global status and is unlikely to be able to forge such deep global commercial ties as Nvidia is set to enter into a period of uncertainty over strategic priorities, pricing, supply agreements and future product commitments. Nvidia has lost a strategic visionary , and it’s set to have repercussions right through the AI trade, given how the chip giant is right at the heart of this technological revolution.

Nvidia’s shares are recovering from that early tumble – they’re down ‘only’ 7.7% – which knocks around $320bn off its valuation.

Nvidia's value has slumped by $888bn this week

More than $575bn has been wiped off Nvidia’s value at the start of trading, as investors react to the departure of Jensen Huang .

Nvidia’s shares have tumbled by over 13% at the start of trading, dropping to $149.79 from $173.73 last night.

They ended last week at $186.64 each. And (by my maths), the company’s valuation has now slumped by $888bn so far this week.

Having ended Friday night worth $4.5tn, Nvidia’s value has now dropped to $3.61bn.

In China, 888 is seen as a lucky number... but not for Huang or Nvidia.

Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson in Portland, Oregon, has looked at the new interim CEO of Nvidia , Colette Kress, who will also continue to serve as chief financial officer.

Luria told Reuters:

double quotation mark Colette Kress is well respected by investors and should be able to guide Nvidia through this challenging period. The task is daunting, as Nvidia has been founder-led since inception and Mr Huang concentrated much of the decision making.

Ben Barringer , head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot, said:

double quotation mark Jensen Huang clearly saw the writing was on the wall and has made the decision to resign as chief executive of Nvidia . This is an important moment in broader financial markets due to the clout that Huang carried, and the fact he had developed Nvidia into the most valuable and influential company in the world. It remains to be seen if Huang will eventually stick around in some sort of ceremonial or non-executive capacity. It would be difficult to see him not retaining some sort of influence over Nvidia, but we do not yet know the full details of the allegations or the outcome of the investigation, and much of what happens next still depends on that. For now, CFO Colette Kress has taken the role on an interim position. While there is no natural successor in place, she is the most obvious internal candidate and will now likely use this time to prove she deserves it full time. She certainly knows the company inside out and has helped develop what is a hugely successful strategy. This doesn’t necessarily harm Nvidia in the short-term. Orders remain strong and the company has a robust earnings outlook. What this news threatens to do is harm the wider AI ecosystem in the longer-term. Huang is hugely influential in the debates around AI regulation and has developed Nvidia into the leader in AI investment and financing. With his voice now removed from the table, and the potential for Nvidia to pivot on its strategy over time, the company may not carry the sway it once did.

Turning to the wider outlook for technology firms, he said:

double quotation mark This news ultimately pours petrol onto what is already a volatile picture for tech companies following the midterm elections. Nvidia and its neocloud partners are likely to bear the initial brunt of this news, while competitors like AMD and Broadcom benefit. That said, this news has the potential to be game changing over the long-term with a key figure out of the picture.

Jensen Huang founded Nvidia in 1993 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priemand “with a vision to bring 3D graphics to the gaming and multimedia markets”.

Huang is the company’s fourth-largest investor with a ⁠stake of about 3.61% and will not ⁠remain on the board.

Here’s some instant reaction to his departure.

Lindsey Stewart , director of institutional investor content at Morningstar, says governance issues and succession planning, long neglected at Nvidia , will become important for other founder-led companies.

double quotation mark The sudden departure of one of the world’s most influential CEOs illustrates just how quickly an unconventional governance structure can become a source of risk, and often real losses, for investors. While Nvidia’s share price rocketed over the last few years, very few people were asking deep questions about CEO succession planning, board composition and challenge, or oversight of geopolitically sensitive aspects of company strategy. Now, all those issues will be front and centre, perhaps not just for Nvidia, but also for other founder-led companies like Anthropic , Meta Platforms and SpaceX.

Nvidia shares now down 10% in premarket trading

Nvidia’s shares are falling deeper into the red in pre-market trading, ahead of the open of Wall Street in less than 25 minutes.

They were already heading for a fall, as investors were unsettled by the news that Nvidia’s board had met last night to consider Jensen Huang’s future.

Now that he has resigned, Nvidia’s shares are down 10.4% – an indication of how trading may proceed when the New York stock market session begins.

Nvidia shares plunge 10%; board pays tribute to Huang and appoints first-ever chair

Nvidia shares have plummeted 10% on the news!

Nvidia paid tribute to Huang, saying:

double quotation mark Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.

Kress, the new interim chief executive, has served as executive vice president and chief financial officer of Nvidia since joining the company in September 2013. The group said she has played a key role in Nvidia’s growth and evolution. Prior to joining, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft .

The Nvidia board also appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever chair. Jones has been an entrepreneur, technology executive, and active venture investor for over 30 years, including serving as chief efficer and executive chairman of Synopsys .

Jones said:

double quotation mark Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position. She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing Nvidia’s strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.

Kress said:

double quotation mark Nvidia’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years. We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.

The US chipmaker will report its third-quarter results on 17 November.

The company issued this statement just now, after its board met last night:

double quotation mark The Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately. Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates.

US trade representative says US 'remains concerned' about Nvidia

US trade representative Jamieson ⁠ Greer ⁠said ⁠the United States “remains ⁠concerned” ​about the tech giant ‌ Nvidia , ‌as the world’s ‌dominant supplier of AI chips grapples with fallout ‌from reports of two extramarital ​affairs involving its longtime ⁠chief executive Jensen Huang .

Greer told CNBC ​on Thursday:

double quotation mark Obviously we ​remain concerned.

Huang has admitted to an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a Chinese businesswoman and former Megaspeed executive, who is accused of spying for Beijing. She has reportedly returned to China.

Wall Street to open lower with tech shares seen sliding

Wall Street is expected to have a bumpy start in just over an hour, with technology shares likely to slide again as the scandal around Nvidia boss Jensen Huang deepens.

Stock futures are extending losses, with the S&P 500 down 0.75%, the tech-heavy Nasdaq 1.5% lower and Dow Jones down 0.2%.

Also, Donald Trump said: “We don’t need a deal with Iran.”

In the second half of a post about corruption in the US, on the social media platform Truth Social, he said:

double quotation mark We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DJT

Oil prices have see-sawed today. Brent crude is now trading 1.5% higher at $93.98 a barrel.

Gold prices have also fallen, by about 2%.

stories.title: Poundland gets more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
stories.summary: A deadline to secure a buyer was set to expire at midnight, but the retailer now has an extra 10 days to find a buyer.
stories.contentStatus: Freely readable article text extracted from publisher page
stories.body:
Published 11 November 2026

Poundland has avoided immediate collapse after a deadline was extended to find a rescue deal.

A deadline to secure a buyer for the retail chain was set to expire at midnight, but a court has given Poundland an extra 10 days to find a buyer.

The discount chain, which has 11,000 employees, has been edging towards administration after being blocked by owners Gordon Brothers from accessing cash in its bank accounts.

A committee of MPs questioned Gordon Brothers following accusations that the investment firm hoped to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 shops and stock piecemeal.

Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just £1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock shops, and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period.

The investment firm, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied the claims.

However, pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

About £50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops.

The BBC understands that Gordon Brothers agreed to release a further £10m to £11m from Poundland's accounts, on top of £11m announced earlier, as the firm seeks to find a new buyer.

Gordon Brothers said it was in talks with three parties for a sale of the whole business, and it had received "several offers from established high street retailers for significant parts of the business".

'Do the right thing'

Following the meeting between MPs on the business and trade committee and representatives of Gordon Brothers, chairman Liam Byrne told the BBC that he was "deeply concerned" and described the firm's behaviour as "much like a wolf on Wall Street, on the British High Street".

"They refused to prioritise protecting jobs and stores over and above their own financial returns," he said.

"It's clear that they've taken millions out of Poundland at a time when they themselves said the business was on a knife edge."

Byrne said the committee's message to Gordon Brothers was to ensure Poundland had "access to the funds that it needs to trade at what should be one of the busiest periods in the year".

He urged Gordon Brothers to "do what is right to save jobs and stores and do that now".

"It's a good business, it's a much-loved business and, particularly in the middle of the cost of living crisis, communities up and down the country rely on access to the kind of stores that it operates," Byrne added.

Views on Poundland performance differ

Views on the chain's performance differ between those running operations and the owners.

Poundland boss Williams told staff last week that like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4%. The sales period included Halloween, but Williams said this was £1.5m ahead of budget.

He added that the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year when there were losses of £68m.

However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading".

It has argued that the best way of securing jobs may be to split up the business and sell chunks of its 600 sites to other retailers.

There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up Poundland shops, which could mean continuing employment for workers at those sites.

The main issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland as a national chain.

stories.title: Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
stories.summary: The first Gemini smartglasses are a collab between Google, Samsung, Gentle Monster, and Warby Parker.
stories.contentStatus: Freely readable article text extracted from publisher page
stories.body:
The first Gemini smartglasses are a collab between Google, Samsung, Gentle Monster, and Warby Parker.

Smartglasses have always faced an uphill road to acceptance. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days . Now, Google is ready to take another swing at “ intelligent eyewear ” for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they’re no impulse buy.

These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered.

Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn’t told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea.

Google says the frames all weigh about 41 grams, which is not terrible but is definitely near the top for glasses generally. They will, naturally, weigh much more when you account for lenses. That will also determine the final pricing. So far, we only have the starting prices for these devices, including non-prescription lenses.

The setup here is similar to the Ray-Ban Meta glasses we’ve seen for a few years. There are no screens in the lenses, but you can interact with the AI system via voice or by activating the integrated camera. The experience should be similar to using Gemini Live on your phone, but it will be a lot easier to fire up the AI. You can say “Hey Gemini” or tap a touch-sensitive area of the frame to start interacting with the robot.

Credit: Gentle Monster Credit: Gentle Monster Since this is the same chatbot that operates across the Google ecosystem, it has access to your data and preferences. You can ask questions and get personalized answers, have Google Maps guide you by voice, or just talk with the AI to kill time. The glasses use custom open-ear speakers to limit distractions for those around you. Google notes the directional microphones should not pick up speech from other people, either. Adding the camera feed is where things get interesting. When the AI can see what you see, it has the potential to do more work on your behalf. Google suggests asking Gemini for recommendations when looking at a bookshelf or glancing at an event poster to have the AI add it to your calendar. The glasses will also support Gemini Guided Vision, which provides conversational audio descriptions for people who are visually impaired. The utility of these devices hinges on Gemini. I would be remiss not to point out that Gemini, like all AI systems, is not infallible. In fact, it can be frustratingly fallible at times. The chatbot still regularly screws up simple things like adding calendar appointments or identifying objects in an image in my testing, and when you don’t have a screen to verify the AI’s output, it may be harder to trust it. These devices will really only make sense if you can rely on Gemini to do things right, and that’s still not a guarantee. Google’s privacy promises All the Gemini-powered glasses from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker feature a 12 MP wide-angle camera capable of shooting photos and video. Google says it has implemented a number of features and limitations to ensure people don’t do creepy things with its intelligent eyewear, and that it doesn’t do creepy things to you—Google claims its approach respects privacy on “both sides of the lens.” For starters, there’s a recording light that is on whenever the camera is active. Like the Meta glasses, Google’s eyewear will detect if the light has been covered up or modified in any way that would prevent it from illuminating. In that event, the glasses will refuse to activate the camera. All Google-powered glasses will have a physical off switch, too.

Credit: Warby Parker Credit: Warby Parker The terms of use for Gemini eyewear also require users to agree not to record people without consent or in sensitive areas. If Google finds out someone has broken those rules, it may remotely disable the glasses. Google is going a bit further in restricting video functionality than Meta, too. Google says it will not allow any apps in the Play Store to live stream video to social media from the glasses (not even YouTube live is supported). The content you record is saved to your gallery, and you can upload that wherever you want, but going live is apparently not on the agenda. Real-time facial recognition is also off the table, according to Google. On the user privacy side, Google says it will not save any images or videos captured by the glasses in your Gemini history. Additionally, none of that data will be used for training AI models or targeting ads. Your voice interactions with Gemini via the glasses are, as with all other Gemini endpoints, not guaranteed the same level of protection. You can delete your chats from the Gemini history, though. Data on the glasses is encrypted, and it remains that way during transit to the cloud. However, it’s not encrypted on Google’s servers. The company does note that it’s working to bring Private AI Compute to glasses, which will isolate data during processing so not even Google can access it. Credit: Gentle Monster Credit: Gentle Monster Anyone looking to get Gemini on their face and test Google’s privacy promise can preorder the glasses from the Gentle Monster and Warby Parker websites. Devices should ship and appear on store shelves on December 10. Importantly, support for these devices is a bit narrow at launch. They will work with all iPhones from the 13 Pro onward. On the Android side, you’ll need a Pixel 7 or newer or a Samsung Galaxy S or Z series device running One UI 9 or later. If you’ve got a cheaper Samsung Galaxy or a device from another OEM, you’re out of luck at the moment. stories.summary: The mayor of London is the most high-profile figure to weigh into the debate over electric vehicle targets On the Today programme this morning, the Labour MP Bell Ribeiro-Addy , a prominent leftwinger, indicated she might vote against legislation to implement the Alan Milburn proposals. She said she was concerned by the idea that the cuts would apply to people already getting sickness and disability benefits, and she said it appeared to be a breach of a promise given last year that people already getting Pip (the personal independence payment) would not lose it. She said: I just don’t think that you get a disabled young person into work by taking away the money that helps them to get into work. The cuts seem to land on young disabled people, and many of them are in college already or already in work. So I don’t see how you fix the first by punishing the second. Milburn said he concluded fundamental change was needed. He said: The whole system needs to be changed, because the system is geared to keeping people inactive when, for young people in particular, it’s all about how can you make them active, get them earning, learning, so that they can rely on a wage rather than on a benefit. So, this is not about cutting one benefit, it’s about rebuilding the system from scratch. He said that he decided existing claimants should be covered by the changes, not just new changes. It’s a big rewriting of the welfare system. And obviously one of the conundrums was, ‘Should this apply to only new claimants?’ I came to the conclusion that wouldn’t be right, not least because you’ve got hundreds of thousands of young people stuck in a benefit system that is trapping them in poverty, giving them no prospect of prosperity or a job.
